title: Lakshmana's warning
hook: a bowstring that shakes a city, and the one person who can calm it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lakshmana's warning set out, carrying Rama's hard message down the mountain. Did you check a promise with a date on it? Day five hundred ninety-two.
screen: `THE PATH VALI TOOK IS NOT CLOSED.`

segments.voice: The monkeys at the gates of Kishkindha see Lakshmana coming and panic. He looks, Valmiki says, like the fire at the end of the world. They scramble up walls and into trees. Some grab boulders and branches, as if that would help. Young Angada goes to meet him and is sent running back inside with the message. Lakshmana walks straight through the city, past the fine houses and gardens, and when he reaches the palace, he twangs his bowstring so loudly that the whole city shakes.
screen: `PANIC AT THE GATES.` → `LIKE THE FIRE AT THE END OF THE WORLD.` → `A BOWSTRING SHAKES THE CITY.`

segments.voice: Inside, Sugriva hears the bowstring, and the party is over. He's frightened, and at first he can't think what he's done wrong; Hanuman has to tell him he let the time slip. He doesn't go out to meet Lakshmana himself. He sends Tara. First idea: of everyone in the palace, Tara is the one who can calm this. Not long ago she was a widow grieving before Rama. Now she walks out to meet his furious brother, and she speaks with complete poise. Why are you angry, prince? she asks. Sugriva has been careless, yes. After years of hardship he's been lost in pleasure. Even great sages have been carried away by desire, she says, and she names Vishvamitra, who once spent years with the celestial dancer Ghritachi and thought it was a single day. Second idea: she tells him the part he hasn't heard. Sugriva hasn't actually forgotten. Orders have already gone out. Armies are already on their way, from mountains and forests everywhere. Come in, she says. Talk to him. Third: watch what her words do. Lakshmana came in furious. He listens, and his anger cools. He doesn't stop being firm, but now he's willing to talk. Here's a quiet turn in the Kishkindha Kanda: the person who cools Rama's warning is the same person whose own warning Vali ignored. Tara has been right twice now. This time somebody listens.
screen: `SUGRIVA SENDS TARA.` · `EVEN SAGES ARE CARRIED AWAY.` · `THE ARMIES ARE ALREADY COMING.` · `THIS TIME SOMEBODY LISTENS.`

segments.voice: Sit, and recall a time someone was angry with you, and fairly. Breathe in, and remember how it felt in your body. Now imagine meeting that anger the way Tara did: calm, honest, admitting the part that's true, explaining the part that isn't. Breathe out. You don't need to rehearse the words. Just let your body learn what calm in front of anger might feel like. The bell holds the time.
Lakshmana's warning. Delivered with a bowstring, and met by Tara: yes, he was careless, and the armies are already coming.
Your line: Lakshmana's warning. Today, if someone's upset with you, admit the true part first, then explain the rest. Day five hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: Storytellers point to Tara here as a model of wise speech; she is remembered for her counsel as much as for her story.

myth: Sugriva goes out himself to face Lakshmana
Tara admits Sugriva has been careless
she owns the fault, then explains that the armies are already called.
Lakshmana's anger cools after Tara speaks
he stays firm, but he's willing to talk.

fork.setup: you're Tara. Rama's furious brother is at the palace door. what do you say?
options: deny that Sugriva did anything wrong.
admit the carelessness, then tell him the armies are already coming.
fork.reveal: she owns the fault, gives the reason, and tells him the truth he hadn't heard: the orders went out.

original.note: Sanskrit lakṣmaṇa: often explained as 'marked with auspicious signs', from lakṣman, a mark or sign.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lakshmana storms in and Sugriva grovels.
what it means: Tara calms him with honesty and news he didn't have.
what a scholar hears: Kishkindha 31–33 have Lakshmana's entry and the bowstring; Tara's speech, with the example of Vishvamitra and Ghritachi, is in Kishkindha 35.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 31–33 (Lakshmana enters Kishkindha)
Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 35 (Tara calms Lakshmana)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering and differ between editions; confirm against the edition the Keeper uses.
Angada going out to meet Lakshmana and returning with the message: confirm in Kishkindha 31.
Tara's example of Vishvamitra and Ghritachi (years taken for a day): paraphrased; confirm.
The text describes Tara as somewhat unsteady from drink when she goes out; the script omits this detail.
Tara's earlier words to Rama after Vali's death (Kishkindha 24) mix grief and reproach; the script now says 'grieving before Rama' rather than 'raging'. Confirm tone.
Etymology of Lakshmana ('having auspicious marks') is the traditional gloss; confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): corrected 'he knows he's in the wrong' (in Kishkindha 32 Sugriva at first sees no fault and Hanuman explains); fixed the garbled 'his fear decides' and 'turns aside Rama's warning' lines; softened howItsDone.
